summary: Record the first executable controller skeleton as a cross-cutting behavioral implementation change requiring full five-stage review before further implementation proceeds.
reason: Revision 9 corrects the six blocker groups carried from the revision-8 Adversarial investigation: PassOccurrence failed-status/result identity coherence, OperationResult review identity coherence, OperationResult outcome/payload compatibility, the missing typed request envelopes, caller-mintable controller-derived identities, and shallowly immutable persistence evidence. The correction adds runtime-validated request dataclasses, makes derived-ID construction/deserialization an internal non-exported boundary, enforces result-envelope coherence, restricts persistence history/evidence to recursively immutable typed values, and adds focused regression coverage. Deferred controller operations, canonical derivation algorithms, a concrete backend, SQLite, and the conformance harness remain outside this first code-bearing boundary. Full review remains reopened at Adversarial.

Deterministic policy defaults to SEPARATED, converts declared isolation requirements into ISOLATED subpasses, and permits FUSED only through exact pre-existing VALIDATED capability permission. findings: SUPPORTED: Revision-9 runtime construction invariants hold for the six corrected blocker surfaces. PassOccurrence rejects semantic_result_id unless status=COMPLETED; the four typed request envelopes enforce runtime types and revision/stage constraints; controller-derived IDs have no public class factories and are absent from the package export surface; OperationResult enforces outcome/payload type and review-id coherence; persistence history/evidence containers reject mutable/untyped members.

SUPPORTED: No additional runtime type, container mutability, enum, boolean, or representability defect was found in the exposed domain/workflow/result/persistence construction surface within this bounded pass.

findings: BLOCKING: Persistence DTOs permit cross-review evidence contamination. AuthoritativeRecord, InitializationCommit, and TransitionCommit validate that history/event/evidence members are immutable typed values, but they do not require review-bearing members such as PassOccurrence or InitializationRecord to match the authoritative review_id. A record/commit for review A can therefore carry immutable evidence for review B while remaining fully well-typed.

SUPPORTED: Revision-9 OperationResult now rejects review-id disagreement for payloads that carry review_id and rejects success outcome/payload type mismatches. Request-side occurrence/gate/revision/snapshot values remain caller expectations to be checked by controller validation rather than trusted authority, and WorkflowDefinition remains internally coherent. No additional contradictory well-typed combination was found in the bounded domain/workflow/result surface.
